selector.rationale: The presence of a firm nodule at the umbilicus that gradually increased in size, became ulcerated and tender, and was diagnosed as a well-differentiated, infiltrating adenocarcinoma, along with the findings of a mass in the right hypochondrium and irregular thickening of the right third of the transverse colon, supports the diagnosis of Sister Mary Joseph nodule, which is a metastatic lesion from a primary cancer, in this case, likely from the transverse colon cancer.

rejected.label: Colorectal cancer
rejected.why: While the patient has a colon cancer, the specific diagnosis of Sister Mary Joseph nodule better explains the umbilical findings.
